findings.finding: The Q3 release is where Easterly gives its first next-year Core FFO guide (Q3 2025 initiated 2026 at $3.05-3.12 against a $3.11 consensus, and the stock fell 4.0%). The 2027 guide must absorb a full year without the FAA Great Lakes Regional Office: the FAA committed to GSA/OMB to vacate 2300 E Devon Ave, Des Plaines by October 2026, its Occupancy Agreement expired 2026-10-20, and it is moving to a 108k SF lease in Rosemont that is 42% smaller. The Des Plaines building is 239,331 SF, about 2.2% of DEA's 10.7M leased SF. On the Q2 call the CEO said 'I would not add additional revenue in your model at this time' and promised an FAA update on this call. The bar for 2027 is unsourced. Management's 2-3% growth target implies ~$3.16-3.19.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: First next-year guide, 2025-10-27: initial 2026 range $3.05-3.12 against a $3.11 consensus, stock -4.0% (baseline history; https://www.tipranks.com/news/the-fly/easterly-government-properties-sees-2026-core-ffo-3-05-3-12-consensus-3-11-thefly). Guide raise on 2026-08-03: +3.82% despite a $0.01 FFO miss. Guidance is the line this name trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Management told the sell side to model no FAA revenue, so the vacancy itself is known. What is not known is how the first 2027 range nets the lost FAA NOI, the opex carry on a 239k SF building that is largely vacant, re-leasing costs and the Loma Linda refinancing against the FDLE delivery and renewal rent growth (mid-to-high teens net effective). If the market had priced a sub-target 2027 guide, the stock would not have bounced 3.1% in the five days into the print, and the sell side would not still be carrying targets 13% above spot.
findings.independence: Two different sources. The FAA's own federal procurement notice gives the vacate date and the OA expiry. The Q2 call summary carries management's 'do not model' comment and the promised update (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-8-3-easterly-government-properties-inc-stock/). WGN/Crain's covers the Rosemont move (https://digital-release.wgnradio.com/?p=1925958, 2023-12-19). The building size is from an older Easterly deal announcement (https://rebusinessonline.com/easterly-government-properties-to-buy-1-5-msf-government-leased-office-portfolio-for-430m/).

findings.finding: The 10-year Treasury sits at 5.09-5.15% (5.13% on 2026-10-21, FRED DGS10), after reaching about 5.2% in late September, its highest since 2007. That raises the cost of refinancing the $127.5M Loma Linda mortgage (3.6%, due summer 2027), which management wants to replace with an investment-grade unsecured issue. On a 7.1-7.3x levered REIT, this is a headwind for the first 2027 interest-expense assumption.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print isolates interest expense. The 2026 initial guide, which management attributed to G&A and timing headwinds, fell 4.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the market sees yields and the stock is 12% off its high. The unpriced part is the company's own assumed refinancing rate in the 2027 range. About 2 points of rate on $127.5M for half a year is roughly $1.3M, or about $0.02-0.03 per share on ~52M diluted shares (hunter arithmetic, not a company number). Hedging on the term loans is not disclosed in what I read.
findings.independence: Macro-to-company proxy. The Loma Linda maturity and the refinancing plan come from the Q2 call summary (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-8-3-easterly-government-properties-inc-stock/). The company has not quantified the 2027 effect.

findings.finding: At $22.50 the stock trades below the price management said unlocks accretive deals ('about $24.50-25.50 unlocks some deals, $26-27 a couple hundred million'), so a 2027 guide is likely to assume little equity-funded external growth. The ATM was refreshed on 2026-08-04 with $215.0M remaining, plus contingent and non-contingent forward options. Management also said development deliveries alone get leverage to target without new equity.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026 guide assumed only $50M of acquisitions and opened 4.0% down. The 2026 raise came with capital-markets execution and the stock rose 3.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, because management published the thresholds. Asked what the ATM buys: it funds acquisitions matched to equity, and at this price management says deals are not accretive, so the program is more likely idle than dilutive. That makes this a growth-assumption point, not a distress signal, which is why it is small.
findings.independence: The price thresholds come from the Q2 call summary (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-8-3-easterly-government-properties-inc-stock/). The ATM terms come from the 8-K. These are different documents.

findings.finding: Unlike the Q3 2025 print on 2025-10-27, which landed during the 43-day shutdown and fell 4.0%, this print comes with the government funded: the Continuing Appropriations Act of 2027 was signed around 2026-09-02 and funds agencies through 2026-12-11. GSA rent-collection risk is not a live Q&A topic this time.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2025-10-27 print fell 4.0% during the shutdown, but that move was attributed to the initial 2026 guide, so the shutdown's share is not separable.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, because the CR is public. The residual is a smaller tail in the call. If shutdown risk were still being priced, a REIT with more than 85% government revenue would be trading with a visible discount into a funding deadline, and the next deadline is 2026-12-11.
findings.independence: Rep. Walberg's release on the CR (https://walberg.house.gov/media/press-releases/walberg-votes-keep-government-open-and-prevent-another-democrat-shutdown). govtschemes is a low-quality outlet, so the signing date is not confirmed against congress.gov.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 reported quarter: the FAA occupied and paid through September (OA to 2026-10-20), so Q3 carries full FAA rent. The new $200M term loan at SOFR+130 repaid revolver borrowings (revolver $43.1M at 6/30 vs $199.1M at 12/31), the SOFR credit-spread adjustment was removed on 2026-07-28, and a $6.4M mortgage was extinguished on 2026-07-14. A Q3 Core FFO at or slightly above the ~$0.775-0.78 implied by the guide is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 printed $0.78 against a $0.79 consensus, a miss, and rose 3.8% on the guide. This name trades the guide, not the quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: It sits inside what the company guided, so it is largely expected. The small upside is the interest savings from the July debt actions, which a $0.01-0.02 FY tightening could reflect. If this were unpriced, the stock would not be trading flat to the guide midpoint.
findings.independence: The debt balances come from the Q2 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1622194/000162219426000026/dea-20260630.htm), which shares its source with the release.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-22 Easterly launched a new brand identity that recasts it as a 'diversified owner, developer and operator of mission-critical properties serving federal, state and local government, and government-adjacent tenants'. That is consistent with its stated goal of 30% non-GSA assets. The release carries no numbers.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public, but rebranding two business days before a print suggests management will frame the call around diversification away from GSA risk, which the FAA move-out makes salient. It carries no quantity, so it is near zero.
findings.independence: The 30% non-GSA target is from the Q2 call summary (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-8-3-easterly-government-properties-inc-stock/).

findings.finding: The Q3 dividend was held at $0.45 (declared 2026-10-22, payable 2026-11-20, record 2026-11-05), an 8.0% yield on spot. That removes the dividend as a print-day question.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2025 dividend reset accompanied the 2025-04-29 print, -4.26%. Since then $0.45 has been held every quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced, since it was declared before the window. It is filed so the judges know the dividend is not in play.

outside_window.finding: Loma Linda $127.5M mortgage at 3.6% matures summer 2027. The refinancing at a ~5.1% 10-year is a 2027 earnings event; only its assumption in the guide is in-window (filed above).
The CR funds the government only through 2026-12-11, so a December shutdown risk to GSA rent timing falls after the window.
